content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text gives UNDERDETERMINED because the sign's sense is left open, which is the kind of single-verse openness K-S2 regulates.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open' -- I weighed reading 'not open' as barring UNDERDETERMINED on an unresolved verse-sense versus reading it as only saying both senses stand; the judge uses 'leaving the sign's sense open' as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.","why":"Because the judge's stated reason for UNDERDETERMINED is that the sign's sense remains open, contrary to K-S2's rule that a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand."}
